ui.heroLede: A self-assessment across the six dimensions of leaders who inspire.
ui.legend: Rate yourself 1 to 5 on each statement, answering honestly about how you lead today rather than how you hope to. A 5 means you strongly agree, a 3 is neutral, and a 1 means you strongly disagree.
ui.footer1: A reflective tool for leaders who want to grow. Scores describe tendencies, not verdicts, and the pattern across the six matters more than any single number.
ui.footer2: Provided by Global Leadership Partners, a non-profit equipping leaders of character to make a positive difference. Replace this line and the mark above with the official logo and footer when you publish.

dimensions.title: Dream Big
dimensions.desc: Vision, and the courage to imagine what could be.
items: I regularly generate ideas that challenge conventional thinking.
I am willing to take calculated risks to achieve meaningful goals.
Others would describe me as more bold than cautious.
When facing problems, I naturally envision what could be possible.
I focus more on long-term vision than short-term details.

dimensions.title: Explain Why
dimensions.desc: Purpose that connects the head and the heart.
items: I am driven by a desire to make a meaningful difference.
I emphasize intrinsic motivation (purpose, growth) over external rewards.
I clearly explain not just what we do, but why it matters.
I communicate purpose in ways that engage both the head and the heart.
I am energized by contributing to causes bigger than myself.

dimensions.title: Build Hope
dimensions.desc: Confidence, example, and reasons to believe.
items: I lead by example and do not ask others to do what I would not do.
I consistently communicate confidence that our vision is achievable.
Others experience me as positive and encouraging.
I demonstrate character and values that earn trust and respect.
I intentionally recognize and celebrate progress and success.

dimensions.title: Show Care
dimensions.desc: Attention, presence, and putting others first.
items: I listen attentively and seek to fully understand others.
I take a genuine interest in the lives of those I lead.
People can count on me during difficult or stressful times.
I create meaningful and memorable moments for others.
I prioritize the needs of others and the team over my own.

dimensions.title: Place Trust
dimensions.desc: Belief in others, and the freedom to deliver.
items: I assume positive intent in others' actions.
I avoid unnecessary perfectionism that limits others.
I trust others to perform at a high level.
I treat mistakes as opportunities for learning and growth.
I delegate outcomes clearly and allow flexibility in how work is done.

dimensions.title: Use Strengths
dimensions.desc: Knowing, and growing, what people do best.
items: I actively seek to understand others' strengths and interests.
I build relationships that help me know people's strengths deeply.
I coach others to develop and apply their strengths.
I regularly align my own work with my strengths.
I intentionally build teams with diverse and complementary strengths.
